Directions. Identify the segment of the sentence which contains the grammatical error. If there is no error mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

As long as Stefan is/ (A) the head of the project,/ (B) he will not be allowing any changes/ (C) in the rules. (D)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 3 i.e., ‘he will not be allowing any changes’- the error lies in this part only.

  • This is a conditional sentence, and in this type of sentence, one sentence depends upon the other because of cause and effect.
  • In this case, this type of sentence follows a special structure.
  • Conditional words are If, even if, until, unless, as soon as, when, while, as long as, after, etc.
  1. Conditional word + subject + v1/v5 + object, subject + will/ shall/ may + v1 + object.
  2. If + subject + v2 + object, subject + would/ should/ could/ might + v1 + object.
  3. If + subject + had + v3 + object, subject + would/ should/ could/ might + have + v3 + object.
  4. Had + subject + v3 + object, subject + would + have + v3 + object.
  • The given sentence follows rule number ‘1’, and according to the rule, the error lies in Part ‘C’.

For example- As long as there is petrol in the car, we will continue driving.

  • In the given sentence, ‘will not be allowing’ is wrongly used instead of ‘will not allow’ in the main clause.

Hence, ‘will not be allowing’ should be replaced by ‘will not allow’.

So, the correct sentence is:

“As long as Stefan is the head of the project, he will not allow any changes in the rules.” 

The conditional expressions, for example- ‘as long as’, ‘so long as’, ‘on condition that’ is used to impose certain conditions or set restrictions to circumstances.

Although he is able to make political enemies with this decision, the Prime Minister Narendra Modi, does not mind doing it for the sake of public welfare.

  1. Although he is liable to make
  2. Although he is accountable for making
  3. Although he is liable from making
questions.explanation:
The adjective ‘able’ means ‘to have skills to do something’, whereas 'liable' means 'at risk of or subject to experiencing or suffering something unpleasant’. Therefore, instead of ‘able’, ‘liable’ should be used.

‘liable’ is followed by preposition ‘to’ or ‘for’.

For example-

  • If you don’t take care of yourself, you’re liable to get sick.
  • He is still liable for repaying his student loan.

‘accountable’ is synonymous to ‘liable’, thus can be used. It is followed by preposition ‘to’ or ‘for’. ‘accountable to’ is used when accountability is towards ‘someone’ and ‘accountable for’ is used when accountability is towards ‘something’.

Thus, alternatives A and B are grammatically correct.

Key Points

  • In Column 1, Statement A says - "Wildlife species will die out and natural ecosystems collapse in the near future"
    • ​Since it talks about an event that 'will' happen 'in the near future', the most apt matching statement in Column 2 for it would be E - "if the climate crisis goes unchecked"
    • This is because the latter also talks about a condition that can give rise to the future event as described by the former
    • Thus A-E is a correctly matched pair
  • In Column 1, Statement B says - "Catastrophe could strike this decade for some species"
    • ​Since it talks about a possibility that an event 'could' happen 'this decade', the most apt matching statement in Column 2 for it would be F - "as key temperature thresholds are crossed"
    • This is because the latter also talks about an event that is quite possible to happen and probably is already in the process of happening and that can satisfy the possible result as mentioned by the former part of the sentence
    • Thus B-F is a correctly matched pair

    • Thus C-D is a correctly matched pair

questions.text: Person X can complete a task in 12 days, and the ratio of the efficiency of X and Y is 3 : 2. X, Y, and Z working together can finish the task in 3 days. If they receive a total payment of Rs. 4800, what is the payment for Z.

Calculation:

Let's denote the efficiency of X = 3a and the efficiency of Y = 2a

where 'a' = efficiencies.

Since,  X complete the task = 12 days

Its total work = 12 × 3a = 36a.

X, Y, and Z together complete the task in 3 days

So their combined efficiency = 36a / 3 days = 12a.

Now, the ratio of the efficiency of X, Y and Z = 3 : 2 : Z

So, Z's efficiency = 12a - (3a + 2a) = 7a.

Now, the total payment is Rs. 4800

Z's share is proportional to his efficiency, which is 7a out of 12a.

Therefore, Z's payment is (7a / 12a) × Rs. 4800 = Rs. 2800.

Hence option number (3) is the right answer.

questions.text: Three cards are drawn one after another with replacement from a pack of cards. What is the probability of getting first card a Jack, second card a black card, and third card an even numbered card?
questions.explanation:
Solution:

With replacement means the card is returned to the deck after it is drawn, which keeps the total number of cards the same for each draw (52 cards in a standard deck).

The first card is a Jack:-

There are 4 Jacks in a pack of 52 cards,

So the probability of drawing a Jack = 4/52 = 1/13

The second card is a black card:-

In a standard deck, there are 26 black cards (13 clubs which are black, and 13 spades which are black).

So the probability of drawing a black card = 26/52 = 1/2

The third card is an even numbered card:-

For this, we consider cards numbered 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 from each suit.

There are 4 suits, so the total number of even-numbered cards in the deck is 20.

So the probability = 20/52 = 5/13

To find the probability of all three of these events occurring together, we multiply their probabilities, since these are independent events:

p = (1/13) × (1/2) × (5/13) = 5/338 

Therefore, the probability of drawing a Jack, then a black card, then an even-numbered card (in that order) from a standard deck of cards, with replacement, is approximately 5/338.

Hence, option(2) is correct.

questions.text: A container contains 96 litres mixture of milk and water out of which 35% is water. 20 litres of the mixture is taken out and 10 litres of milk and 16 litres of water are added to the remaining mixture. Find the difference between the quantity of milk and water in the final mixture after replacement.
questions.explanation:
Given :

Initial quantity of the mixture = 96 litres

Initial quantity of water in the mixture = 35%

20 litres of the mixture is taken out and 10 litres of milk and 16 litres of water are added to the remaining mixture.

Formulation : 

Quantity of the milk after removal of mixture = Initial quantity of milk × [(1 - Part of mixture which is removed)]

Calculation :

Initial quantity of water in the mixture = 35% × 96 = 33.6 litres

Initial quantity of milk in the mixture = 96 - 33.6 = 62.4 litres

Part of total mixture which is removed = 20/96 = 5/24

Total quantity of (milk + water) in the final mixture = 96 × [1 - (5/24)] + 10 + 16 = 102 litres

Final quantity of milk after replacement = 62.4 × [1 - (5/24)] + 10 = 59.4 litres

Final quantity of water after replacement = 102 - 59.4 = 42.6 litres

Required difference = 59.4 - 42.6 = 16.8 litres

Hence, the correct answer is 16.8 litres.

questions.text: A is as efficient as B and C together are. A and B can together do a piece of work in 12 hours and C can do the same work in 36 hours. The time required by B to complete the whole work alone is?
questions.explanation:
GIVEN: 

the efficiency of A = efficiency of B and C together

time taken by A and B to complete = 12 hours

time taken by C to complete = 36 hours

CONCEPT:

The time required to complete the work is the reciprocal of the fraction of work done in one time period (one hour).

EXPLANATION:

(A + B)'s one hour work = \(\frac{1}{12}\)

C's one hour work = \(\frac{1}{36}\)

(A + B + C)'s one hour work = \(\frac{1}{12}+\frac{1}{36}=\frac19\)

replace B + C with A as the efficiency of both is the same

(2A)'s one hour work = \(\frac19\)

A's one hour work = \(\frac{1}{18}\)

B's one hour work = \(\frac{1}{12}-\frac{1}{18}=\frac{1}{36}\)

∴ time taken by B to complete the whole work = 36 hours

 

Let total work = 36 (L.C.M of 12, 36)

(A + B)'s one hour work = 3

C's one hour work = 1

(A + B + C)'s one hour work = 4

replace B + C with A as the efficiency of both is the same

(2A)'s one hour work = 4

A's one hour work = 2

B's one hour work = 3 - 2 =1

∴ time taken by B to complete the whole work = \(\frac{36}{1}=36 hours\)
